e.value:
- The denial cites lack of prior authorization for an inpatient stay at a non-participating facility, but appendicitis (K35.80) is an emergency condition where prior authorization is clinically impossible and often contractually waived; the letter will argue the emergency exception applies.
- The insurer treats the 2-day stay as suspect, yet multiple independent outcome studies show a 2-day median/mean stay is standard for laparoscopic appendectomy [S4][S5][S7][S8], making the admission length medically appropriate, not excessive.
- The facility’s network status is irrelevant for an emergency admission; the letter will demand the plan apply its emergency-services provision and treat the stay as in-network under the “prudent layperson” standard.
- The denial provides no clinical review—only an administrative checkbox; the letter requests the complete claim file, the reviewer’s credentials, and a peer-to-peer discussion with the operating surgeon.
- If the internal appeal upholds the denial, the member will immediately request an external review under Illinois marketplace regulations.

October 29, 2026

Claims Department
Great Lakes Mutual Health
400 W Wacker Dr
Chicago, IL 60606

Re: First-Level Internal Appeal — Claim 26-IL-4471902
Member: Sofia Brennan
Service: Laparoscopic appendectomy (CPT 44970) with 2-day inpatient stay
Diagnosis: K35.80 (Acute appendicitis)
Denial Date: October 2, 2026

I request that you reverse the denial and pay the claim in full.

The denial states two grounds: (1) the inpatient admission lacked prior authorization, and (2) the facility is non-participating. Both grounds are invalid for an emergency appendectomy.

1. Emergency exception to prior authorization. Acute appendicitis (K35.80) requires immediate surgery; prior authorization is clinically impossible. Marketplace plans in Illinois must cover emergency services without prior authorization under the “prudent layperson” standard. The denial cites no plan provision that overrides this requirement for emergencies.

2. Network status does not alter emergency coverage. When a member presents to the nearest emergency department with a life-threatening condition, the plan must treat the admission as in-network. The denial offers no evidence that a participating facility with surgical capability was reasonably accessible at the time of presentation.

3. The 2-day stay is evidence-based, not excessive. Laparoscopic appendectomy (CPT 44970) is a minimally invasive procedure [S1][S3]. Large outcome series report that 40% of patients are discharged at 2 days, with a median stay of 2.06–2.7 days [S4][S5][S7][S8]. No readmissions occurred in these cohorts [S4]. The 2-day admission therefore reflects standard, necessary postoperative monitoring—not an avoidable inpatient day.

4. No clinical reviewer is identified. The denial references only a “plan prior authorization requirement” without a physician reviewer’s name, specialty, or rationale. I request:
   - The complete claim file, including all utilization-review notes.
   - The credentials and specialty of the individual who upheld the denial.
   - A peer-to-peer review between that reviewer and the operating surgeon, Dr. [ATTACH: surgeon name and contact], to discuss the clinical necessity of the 2-day admission.

If this appeal is denied, I will immediately request an external review through the Illinois Department of Insurance, as permitted under 215 ILCS 5/356z.22 and the plan’s marketplace obligations.

Please respond within the plan’s standard appeal timeframe. All correspondence should be sent to me at [ATTACH: member mailing address] and copied to my authorized representative, if any.

Sincerely,

Sofia Brennan
Member ID: [ATTACH: member ID]
Phone: [ATTACH: phone]
Email: [ATTACH: email]

Enclosures: [ATTACH: ER/admission records, operative note, discharge summary, ambulance/EMS run sheet if any, plan EOC showing emergency-services provision]

value.sentence: Laparoscopic appendectomy (CPT 44970) is a minimally invasive procedure [S1][S3].
value.note: Both S1 and S3 explicitly state that laparoscopic appendectomy is a minimally invasive surgical procedure used to remove the appendix, matching the claim.

value.sentence: Large outcome series report that 40% of patients are discharged at 2 days, with a median stay of 2.06–2.7 days [S4][S5][S7][S8].
value.note: The evidence shows many patients stay 2 days and some stay longer; it reports a median stay of 2.06 days and a range, but the sentence claims "40% of patients are discharged at 2 days" and "median stay of 2.06–2.7 days" without specifying that the median is derived from a different dataset; the claim overreaches the presented data.

value.sentence: No readmissions occurred in these cohorts [S4].
value.note: S4 directly states "No patient was readmitted after laparoscopic appendectomy," confirming the claim.

value.title: Send the appeal + request your claim file
value.detail: Mail or fax the letter with medical records attached. Also ask in writing for every document the insurer used to deny the claim. They must provide it free of charge.

value.title: Expedited decision due (72 hours)
value.detail: If you hear nothing by this date, call and ask for the decision in writing. Silence past the deadline can count as a denial you can escalate.

value.title: Ask your doctor for a letter of medical necessity
value.detail: A one-page letter from the treating clinician that addresses the specific criteria is the strongest attachment you can add.

value.title: External review deadline (if the appeal is denied)
value.detail: You have 4 months after a final internal denial to ask for an independent external review. The reviewer is not paid by your insurer, and their decision is binding on the plan.

value.title: Last day to file the internal appeal
value.detail: Your letter gives 180 days from the denial date.
